text:
maria: Hey folks — first day here 👋. I'm on Ubuntu 22.04 (company laptop) and trying to bootstrap the dev env. Running into Docker socket permission errors when running compose from the repo and asdf node installs keep failing with openssl errors. Who should I bug for a quick hand?

ryan: welcome Maria! for the docker socket issue, try adding your user to the docker group first: `sudo usermod -aG docker $USER` then log out/in. If that doesn't work check `/var/run/docker.sock` perms.

sophia: +1 to that. Also on Ubuntu we usually install Homebrew (linuxbrew) for some dev tools instead of apt for parity with macs. steps I use: `/bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/install/HEAD/install.sh)"` then add brew to PATH per the installer output.

maria: thanks — I tried usermod and logged out but still get `Permission denied` on `/var/run/docker.sock`. ls -l shows `srw-rw---- 1 root docker` and I'm in docker group?

sam: did you restart the docker service after adding the group? `sudo systemctl restart docker` and make sure your session is re-evaluated (`newgrp docker` or full logout). sometimes GUI login managers keep the old groups until full logout.

maria: ah `newgrp docker` fixed it, thanks.

maria: re: asdf / node install — error was `openssl incompatible: cannot find OpenSSL` when building node 16. I tried `sudo apt-get install libssl-dev` but the install still broke.

ben: on Ubuntu we prefer to install openssl dev via apt and point asdf to brew openssl if you're also using linuxbrew. For me this flow works (one-liners):

```
# install system deps
sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y build-essential libssl-dev libbz2-dev libreadline-dev libsqlite3-dev curl git
# install brew (if not already)
/bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/install/HEAD/install.sh)"
# make sure brew is on PATH (follow installer output)
# then install openssl via brew and tell node build where it is
brew install openssl@1.1 pkg-config
export LDFLAGS="-L$(brew --prefix openssl@1.1)/lib"
export CPPFLAGS="-I$(brew --prefix openssl@1.1)/include"
# asdf reshim / reinstall node
asdf plugin-add nodejs https://github.com/asdf-vm/asdf-nodejs.git || true
asdf install nodejs 16.20.0
asdf global nodejs 16.20.0
```

ben: also you'll want to run `asdf reshim` after installs.

maria: awesome — I'll try that. any tips for bootstrapping dotfiles and env vars? repo has a `./bootstrap.sh` but it expects `~/.ssh/id_ed25519` and a `.env.local` file.

ryan: clone dotfiles (link in handbook) and run `./bootstrap.sh` — it will prompt for keys. For secrets we use 1Password CLI (op); check the README in infra-tools for how to sign in. There is a `env.example` in the repo; copy to `.env.local` and populate values. We do NOT commit credentials.

sophia: if you prefer not to create keys locally, we can add your laptop to the onboarding access list temporarily so infra can push an SSH key for you. ping @ben if you want that.

maria: how do I use GPG for commit signing? VS Code Remote wants agent forwarding and I can't get it to pick up my gpg key from GNOME Keyring.

sam: for GPG on Linux I usually: install `gnupg`, import key, then enable ssh/gpg agent in `~/.bashrc` or use `gpgconf --launch gpg-agent`. If using VS Code Remote, enable `remote.SSH.forwardAgent` and `gpg-agent` socket forwarding. There's some writeup in the handbook under "developer workstation".

infra-bot: [provisioning] Maria's laptop: onboarding checklist created. If you need temporary infra access open a ticket at #help (tag: onboarding).

maria: thanks infra-bot :raised_hands: — small follow up: when I run `./bootstrap.sh` it expects `asdf install` to find a `.tool-versions`. repo has one in `server/.tool-versions` but not at root. Should I copy it?

ben: yup copy the repo tool-versions to root or point asdf via `ASDF_ENV_FILE` if you have a custom wrapper. Common pattern: `cp server/.tool-versions .` so root asdf picks it up for local dev. We try to keep the canonical .tool-versions in the service folders but many folks copy to root for convenience.

maria: got it — copying that fixed node install. Last question: any recommended quickchecks before pinging eng for a permissions/CI run?

ryan: run `make ci-local` (short version of CI) and `scripts/check-env` (the repo has a helper that checks required env vars). If those pass then open a PR and ping your buddy. :thumbsup:

maria: thanks everyone — smooth onboarding so far. tagging notes here so future new-hires can search. :)

sophia: welcome aboard! drop me a message if you want a quick pairing session to go through the codebase and how we run local stacks.

maria: will do — appreciate the help!
